newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African business mulls action on planned strike.
newsitem.headline: S.African business mulls action on planned strike.

text.p: The South African Chamber of Business (Sacob) said on Wednesday that business figures were mulling legal action against a planned general strike by South Africa's largest trade union federation on May 12.
The Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) is planning the action to protest over upcoming employment legislation.

"Organised business is currently considering its legal options regarding the national strike planned for May 12," Sacob director-general Raymond Parsons said in a speech for delivery to the Sandton (municipality) Chamber of Commerce and Industry.
"We must not advance labour standards at the expense of economic efficiency," he added.
Parsons said if South Africa wanted to meet its economic targets for growth and job creation it would have to concentrate on creating a flexible labour market.
"The need to address labour market flexibility is crucial to creating new jobs in an environment where the stripping of protective barriers has already contributed to labour shedding," Parsons said.
